newsitem.title: USA: US senators to back bill banning landmines - Post.
newsitem.headline: US senators to back bill banning landmines - Post.

text.p: Fifty six U.S. senators, including a few conservative Republicans and six Vietnam combat veterans, will announce on Thursday their intention to pass a law banning the use of land mines by U.S. forces, the Washington Post reported in Thursday editions.
President Bill Clinton has opposed a unilateral landmine ban because of objections by the Defence Department.

The Clinton administration is pressing instead for a global ban by the year 2001 on the stockpiling, production and use of such weapons, which kill tens of thousands of people, most of them innocent civilians, around the world every year.

The newspaper quoted a White House official as saying that it was too early to know how Clinton would respond to a unilateral ban. In January, he announced a permanent ban on U.S. production of mines to other countries and said the United States would destroy millions of stockpiled mines that do not self-destruct.
The Senate bill is being co-sponsored by Sen. Patrick Leahy, a Vermont Democrat, and Sen. Chuck Hagel, a Nebraska Republican, a former Army sergeant who was wounded twice by landmines in Vietnam.

Clinton administration officials are due to meet on Thursday with counterparts in Canada to discuss ways to narrow differences over a Canadian initiative for a global treaty banning use, export, transfer and production of landmines.
